previous_result.summary:
Fixed. The failure was environmental, not code — no implementation file was touched.

## What changed

**`tasks/graph-pan.md`** — front matter only (in content terms):

```
setup: npm ci --prefix desktop
test_commands: npm run typecheck --prefix desktop
```

replacing `test_commands: npx --prefix desktop tsc --noEmit -p desktop`. The worktree carries no `desktop/node_modules`, so `npx` fell through to the registry decoy package named `tsc` and exited 1. `setup:` is the pipeline's own mechanism (`run_setup`, `aidev/pipeline.py:3199`) and auto-grants `Bash(npm ci:*)`. `npm run typecheck` resolves `tsc` from `desktop/node_modules/.bin` with cwd inside `desktop/`, and unlike `tsc -p desktop` (a solution file, `"files": []`) it actually checks `src/domains/**` and the `.tsx`.

**Side effect I could not avoid, and you should know about:** that file was CP949-encoded (as every file in `tasks/` is). The Edit tool decodes as UTF-8, so a front-matter edit turned the Korean body into `U+FFFD`. I removed and rewrote the file whole, in UTF-8, with the requirement text restored verbatim from the slice's requirement. Net effect on the body: byte encoding changed CP949 → UTF-8, wording identical. This is also a fix rather than a regression — `start_slice` reads the requirement with `read_text(encoding="utf-8")` strict (`aidev/pipeline.py:5308`), which the CP949 bytes would have raised on.

## Verification

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm ci --prefix desktop --no-audit --no-fund` | PASS 45.5s |
| `npm run typecheck --prefix desktop` (the new declared command) | PASS 8.1s |
| `npm test --prefix desktop` — typecheck + compiles and runs `layout.test.ts` | PASS 11.9s |
| `npx --prefix desktop tsc --noEmit -p desktop` (the old declared command, still what this run's `AIDEV_VERIFY_COMMANDS` holds) | PASS 1.8s |

`git status` is clean apart from `tasks/graph-pan.md` — `node_modules` stays untracked.

## Two things worth flagging

1. **How I installed the dependencies.** Plain `npm` i
